title: Power Display: Inconsistent triple monitor detection after Maximum Compatibility update

judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with the same display model across DP and HDMI, tracing Windows display inventory and Power Display DDC/CI responses.
judgment.rationale: Latest investigation narrows the symptom: two Pixio PX274P displays share a model/name; the DP-connected monitor responds, while the failure follows the HDMI connection after swapping and persists even when the other monitor is removed. The maintainer says Power Display relies on Windows DDC/CI requests. This does not prove whether Windows or Power Display causes the missing response.
evidence: Reporter uploaded a PowerToys bug-report ZIP on 2026-10-13; the maintainer saw two same-model displays and one not responding to DDC/CI requests.
Reporter says one Pixio PX274P on DP works and the other on HDMI fails.
After swapping connections, the problem follows HDMI and remains when the third monitor is removed.
Maintainer states Power Display uses Windows native DDC/CI API.

fix_assessment.rationale: A discovery or WMI/DDC route mismatch is plausible, but the current thread combines direct and USB-C-connected monitor reports and lacks the exact topology needed to choose a safe fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve every attached display through Power Display discovery and routing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A display may be lost between the Windows DisplayConfig inventory and Power Display's WMI/DDC controller classification, particularly on a dock/USB-C path; duplicate friendly names alone are less likely because current monitor identity is based on a DevicePath.
plan: Compare DisplayConfigInventory.GetAllMonitorDisplayInfo output with MonitorManager.DiscoverFromAllControllersAsync classification for the reporter's exact topology.
Trace each display by DevicePath through MonitorIdentity.FromDevicePath and the WMI/DDC route; do not use friendly name or model ID as a unique monitor key.

If a path is dropped or capability-mapped incorrectly, preserve each distinct physical path and report unsupported controls per monitor; add tests for identical model/friendly names and docked displays.
verification: With the reporter's three-monitor topology, verify that every display Windows enumerates appears in Power Display, and that only genuinely unsupported brightness/contrast/volume controls are disabled.

confidence.rationale: The current source separates monitor identity from friendly name, but the report does not identify whether Windows, DisplayConfig, or a Power Display controller omits the third monitor.

issue_context.summary: Power Display shows inconsistent monitor/control detection in a multi-monitor setup; latest evidence says the DDC/CI failure follows the HDMI connection rather than a specific Pixio monitor.
known_information: Initial report uses v0.100.2 and Windows build 26200.8973; later logs were provided on 2026-10-13.
Maintainer found two Pixio PX274P displays in logs; one does not respond to DDC/CI requests.
The DP-connected device works and HDMI-connected device fails; after swapping, failure follows HDMI, even when used alone.
Power Display sends DDC/CI messages through the Windows native API, per maintainer comment.
A separate commenter also reported missing USB-C-hub displays; that report is not established as the same cause.
inferences: A Windows/HDMI DDC/CI communication or capability-routing issue is plausible; the failure following the HDMI path narrows but does not prove the boundary.
The duplicate friendly/model name did not alone establish an identity collision; inspected source uses device path for identity.
issue_context.analysis: The original request for topology was substantially answered by connection swap testing. Avoid asking the reporter to repeat it; maintainers can compare Windows DisplayConfig inventory and DDC/CI responses across DP/HDMI for the identified monitor.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue and all 13 comments, including the attached diagnostic ZIP discussion and the connection swap experiment.
Previously inspected Power Display discovery and MonitorIdentity: display identity derives from Windows DevicePath and controller capability routing uses DDC/CI/WMI.
No covering PR or confirmed fix was identified.

actions.note: Queues the design workflow for maintainer approval; no upstream write occurs.
actions.label: Review Power Display DDC/CI path investigation

reproduce.expected_result: Each Windows-enumerated monitor is represented, and DDC/CI controls are enabled only when the corresponding display responds.
steps: Confirm Windows Display Settings enumerates the monitor on each connection.
Open Power Display and record monitor discovery and available controls for DP.
Repeat on HDMI and capture whether the Windows DDC/CI request receives a response.
Compare device paths and controller classification; do not rely on friendly name alone.
reproduce.version_requirements: Current supported build; Pixio PX274P or equivalent DDC/CI monitor
prerequisites: Use a test setup with the same monitor connected first by DP and then by HDMI.
Keep Windows display topology and monitor power unchanged between runs.
